name: גָּד
summary: Jacob’s seventh son, born to him by Zilpah, Leah’s maid, and the tribe that came from him, which camped on the south with Reuben and set out in Reuben’s camp, its host under Eliasaph son of Deuel (Num 2:14; 10:18–20), and took its land east of the Jordan in Gilead; and Gad the prophet, David’s seer. Leah named the child from the noun גַּד, crying בָּא גָד, “fortune has come” (Gen 30:11). Jacob’s blessing turns the name to the troop: “Gad, a גְּדוּד will raid him, but he will raid at their heel” (Gen 49:19).

evidence.note: “Leah said, בָּא גָד, fortune has come, and called his name גָּד.” The written text has בְּגָד, “with fortune”.
The same word as a noun: a table set לַגַּד, for Fortune.
“גָּד גְּדוּד יְגוּדֶנּוּ וְהוּא יָגֻד עָקֵב”: the name heard as “troop”, with גְּדוּד and the verb גּוּד.
The sons of Zilpah, Leah’s maid: Gad and Asher.
Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.
Reuben and Gad, with much cattle, ask for the land of Gilead.
Moses: “Blessed is he who enlarges Gad; he dwells as a lion.”
Gadites who came to David were men of war, with faces like lions and swift as gazelles: the gentilic גָּדִי.
Of the tribe of Gad twelve thousand were sealed.
“Gad the prophet said to David, Do not stay in the stronghold.”
Gad the prophet, David’s seer, brings Yahweh’s three choices after the census.
The acts of David are written in the words of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet and Gad the seer.

evidence.locator: p. 135, GD IV and GD V
evidence.note: Punic names of the same kind: gdʿštrt “Astarte is my good luck”, nʿmgdʾ “May my luck be good!”, and gd, the god Fortune.

note: Takes c.ao.af (the name, 77 tokens) and the gentilic גָּדִי “Gadite” (c.ao.ag, 16 tokens), which TIPNR lists as a form of Gad@Gen.30.11. c.ao.af also holds the place names Baal-gad (Jos 11:17; 12:7; 13:5) and Migdal-gad (Jos 15:37) and the noun at Gen 30:11 (בָּא גָד), so its count is not all the person. Gadi (c.ao.ah), Gaddi (c.ao.aj) and Gaddiel (c.ao.ak) are other names of the same word, not written here. The verb of Gen 49:19 is גּוּד (c.az.aa), another root key.
